hypotheses.text: Anterior temporal pole sparing vs. involvement in biallelic NOTCH3-related small vessel disease is strictly dictated by the functional class of the variant: biallelic loss-of-function/null variants spare the anterior temporal lobes, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving or missense variants produce classic anterior temporal pole hyperintensities resembling CADASIL.
hypotheses.rationale: The conflict in the literature between cohorts observing strict temporal pole sparing (Stellingwerff 2022, Tasharrofi 2024) and those reporting temporal pole lesions (Iruzubieta 2024, Luo 2026) can be resolved by distinguishing loss-of-function variants from cysteine-involving or EGFr missense alleles.

evidence.text: A comprehensive study of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants verified distinct genotype-phenotype correlations: biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with periatrial white matter volume loss, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) manifest as CADASIL spectrum phenotype with typical deep and anterior temporal white matter lesions.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

evidence.text: In 3 pediatric patients presenting with early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by biallelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants, brain MRI showed extensive white matter abnormalities, basal ganglia lacunes, and calcifications, but the anterior temporal lobes were strictly spared.

source.quote: The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

hypotheses.text: Biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 mutations cause periatrial leukomalacia-like white matter volume loss and microcalcifications rather than the confluent anterior temporal pole T2 hyperintensities typical of dominant CADASIL.
hypotheses.rationale: Neuroimaging differences between dominant CADASIL and recessive NOTCH3 loss-of-function extend beyond anterior temporal sparing to include specific positive hallmarks (periatrial volume loss, microbleeds, microcalcifications).

evidence.text: Expert neuroradiological analysis showed that biallelic loss-of-function variants produce periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, unlike the deep white matter lesions without volume loss seen in cysteine-involving variants.

hypotheses.text: Recessive homozygous cysteine-sparing missense variants outside loss-of-function null mutations (such as in EGFr19) present with temporal pole white matter hyperintensities and exceptionally high cerebral microbleed burden compared to classic CADASIL.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifies whether all recessive cases lack temporal pole lesions, or whether homozygous missense non-cysteine variants in EGFr domains can still affect anterior temporal lobes while dramatically elevating cerebral microbleed count.

evidence.text: Two siblings with a homozygous cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 missense variant in EGFr19 (c.3373G>A, p.Glu1125Lys) exhibited confluent periventricular and temporal pole white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas grade 3) along with significantly elevated cerebral microbleed density.

source.title: Homozygous NOTCH3 c. 3373G> A (p.(Glu1125Lys)) in a consanguineous Chinese family presenting with vestibular migraine and epilepsy: Expanding the genotype …
source.quote: MRI showed confluent periventricular and temporal pole white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas grade 3) and numerous deep CMBs, particularly in the basal ganglia and cerebellum. Quantitatively, total CMB density was higher compared with controls (mean 2.15 counts/cm³ vs. 0.4 ± 0.2 counts/cm³; p = 0.008).

new_directions.question_text: Does the age of MRI assessment explain the reported temporal pole involvement in the Moroccan biallelic NOTCH3 null patient (Ouskri 2025) versus strict sparing in younger pediatric null cohorts (Stellingwerff 2022)?
new_directions.rationale: Ouskri et al. assessed a 12-year-old patient with homozygous frameshift variant and described temporal pole involvement, whereas Stellingwerff et al. examined infants presenting at 9-14 months; age-dependent progression of leukoencephalopathy may account for discrepancy in loss-of-function phenotypes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of cerebral microcalcifications and periatrial volume loss for distinguishing biallelic NOTCH3 loss-of-function leukoencephalopathy from HTRA1-related CARASIL?
new_directions.rationale: While alopecia and lumbago differentiate CARASIL clinically, neuroradiological discriminators between these two childhood/early-adulthood recessive arteriopathies remain unquantified.
